S24.02.needs: a file to upload (upload one first with New > Upload file if the Library is empty)
S24.02.note: The tab is labelled Uploads, not an uploaded-files view name; the filter is origin uploaded.
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Uploads tab in the row of tabs under the search box.
Look that only files you uploaded are listed (no files the assistant made).

S24.03.needs: an account that already has a generated file (for example an image or document made in a chat)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Generated files tab in the row of tabs under the search box.
Look that only files the assistant produced are listed, and that uploads are not.

S24.04.needs: an account with at least one artifact made in a chat
S24.04.note: The tile label is built as Open <name> in code, so the exact tile text depends on the artifact name.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Artifacts tab.
Click a tile labelled Open followed by an artifact name; the artifact opens in the Library viewer.
Look that the list shows only your artifacts and that each one opens.

S24.05.needs: an account with at least one image
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Images tab.
Click an image tile (its label is Open followed by the file name). The image opens in a viewer dialog named after the file, with Zoom in and Zoom out buttons.
Look that the image is shown in the viewer and that the Images tab lists images only.

S24.06.needs: an account with at least one video
S24.06.note: The video player is a standard video element with controls (test id library-video-player).
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Videos tab.
Click a video tile (label Open followed by the file name).
In the viewer, press the play control on the video and look that it plays.

S24.08.needs: a signed-in account with a few library files
S24.08.note: No separate Recent view exists in the Library; the recent list is the Add from library submenu, sorted by modified. The exact label of the + button was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Open a chat (or New chat) and click the + button beside the message box.
Hover or click Add from library.
Look at the list: it shows your most recently changed library files, newest first.
Click Browse all at the bottom to compare with the full Library sorted by Modified.
S24.08.where: Chat composer > (+) menu > Add from library

S24.12.needs: an account with a few files
S24.12.note: These are icon-only buttons; their names come from the title and aria labels.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar and note that files show as tiles.
Click the List view icon button at the right of the filter row.
Look that files now show as rows with a name, date and size.
Click the Grid view icon button and look that tiles return.
S24.12.where: Sidebar > Library > Grid view / List view (icon buttons at the top right, in the group Library layout)

S24.13.needs: an account with several named files
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the box that says Search files and projects and type part of a file name.
Wait a moment; the list narrows to matching names.
Clear the box and look that all files return. A search with no match shows No matches.
S24.13.where: Sidebar > Library > search box (Search files and projects)

S24.14.needs: an account with an image, a video and a document
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click Documents, then Images, then Videos in the row of tabs.
Look that each tab shows only that file type.
Click All to return to everything.

S24.15.needs: an account with both uploaded and generated files
S24.15.note: Only upload and generated origins are filters. No connector or provider filter was found in LibraryView.tsx.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click Uploads, then Generated files in the row of tabs.
Look that each tab shows only files from that source.
Click All to return to everything.

S24.19.needs: an account with several files of different names, sizes and types
S24.19.note: On narrow screens only the icon shows; its name is Sort by plus the current option.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the sort button at the top right of the filter row (it shows Modified on wide screens).
Choose Name, then Size, then Type from the menu.
Look that the order changes each time; Modified sorts newest first.
S24.19.where: Sidebar > Library > sort button (shows Modified) > Name / Size / Type

S24.27.needs: a document file in the Library and at least one project (the dialog says you have no projects if none exist)
S24.27.note: The menu item appears only for document types the app accepts as project files.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
On a document row, click the three-dot button labelled Actions for <file name>.
Click Add to project. A dialog titled Add to project opens.
Click a project in the list, then open that project and look for the file.
S24.27.where: Sidebar > Library > (row) Actions for <file name> > Add to project

S24.28.note: The attach row label is built as Attach <file name> in code.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Actions for <file name> button on a file row, then Add to chat.
Look that a new chat opens with the file attached in the message box.
Alternatively, in any chat click the + button, then Add from library, then Attach <file name>.
S24.28.where: Sidebar > Library > (row) Actions for <file name> > Add to chat

S24.29.needs: a file that was created inside a chat (an uploaded or generated file from a conversation)
S24.29.note: The item is shown only when the file has a conversation id.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Actions for <file name> button on a file that came from a chat.
Click Open chat.
Look that the chat the file came from opens.
S24.29.where: Sidebar > Library > (row) Actions for <file name> > Open chat

S24.33.needs: a signed-in account (the numbers come from the account's plan)
S24.33.note: The line is shown only when the server returns a storage figure; the allowance part is shown only when a limit is returned.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Read the small line under the Library heading, for example 'X of Y file storage used'.
Read the second line about file downloads used this month if it is shown.
Upload or delete a file, return to Library, and look that the number changes.
S24.33.where: Sidebar > Library > the line under the Library heading (storage used)

labels.text: Deleted files wait here for 30 days before they are removed for good.

S24.34.needs: a file in the Library that you are willing to delete and restore
S24.34.note: Delete asks for confirmation first; the copy says deleted files stay restorable for 30 days.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Open a file's Actions for <file name> menu and click Delete; confirm in the dialog.
Click the trash icon labelled Recently deleted in the filter row.
Open the file's Actions menu, click Restore, then return to All and look that the file is back.
S24.34.where: Sidebar > Library > Recently deleted (trash icon) > Restore

labels.text: This file is unavailable right now. Try again later, or remove this entry.

S24.35.needs: a deleted file (for Kept until); a file whose stored copy is missing (for the unavailable message), which is hard to set up
S24.35.note: No word 'expired' is shown; the expired state appears as Kept until and as the unavailable message. The unavailable case is hard to reproduce on purpose.
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar, then the trash icon labelled Recently deleted.
Look at each deleted file's line for Kept until and a date.
For a file whose content cannot be loaded, look for the line This file is unavailable right now. Try again later, or remove this entry.
S24.35.where: Sidebar > Library > Recently deleted (for Kept until); a file row that cannot load (for the unavailable message)
